Params: {3: 'The sea is placid on the way back, peaceful in a way that borders on mockery.'}
{3: 'Adelyde does not remember piloting the Kelpie back to the manor. What stays with her is the torrent of emotion churning inside her chest.'}
{3: 'In the early morning, every window of the manor is dark except for the one in the Chief Risk Control Officer's office. Only when Adelyde returns does that light finally go out.'}

{3: 'She has already rehearsed the whole confrontation in her mind: how Rusalka would scold her, perhaps even meet her on the training ground, and how she would parry every accusation, turn every move back on her teacher...'}
{3: 'But Rusalka does not come. Adelyde is left with no one to fight.'}
{3: 'The armory doors close behind her, shutting out all sound from the manor.'}
{3: 'Her consciousness connects. The physical world slips away, and the familiar gray space takes shape around her.'}
{3: 'The Helio crest still rules the vaulted ceiling, just as it did a decade ago, cold and unyielding.'}
{3: 'And in the middle of the space, the heavy cross cannon hangs suspended in silence.'}
{3: 'The weapon that she once had to break down into separate pieces just to carry as a child, that took her two full years to drag a hundred meters across the training floor.'}
{3: 'Adelyde steps forward and lifts it with one hand.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Training mode. Run it on max difficulty, no assists.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The cannon spits flame, and each target crumbles under the assault. Her form is unerring, as though programmed, each shot driving home to the mark.'}
{3: 'Time blurs away. At last, the final target explodes into scattered light.'}
{3: 'Panels flicker to life on all sides, enclosing her.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'A hundred meters, a thousand... I can reach anywhere now.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'If they sent me into battle right now, I wouldn't flinch.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The light panels hang in silence. None of them hold an answer.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Ten years. I spent ten years getting strong... to win.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'A sense of absurdity grips her, even stronger than anger. A great void opens in her chest, a darkness so absolute that not even light can escape it.'}
{3: 'It tries to consume everything: victory, fame, strength... None of the concepts that once carried weight can fill that emptiness.'}
{3: 'Adelyde draws the virtual pistol from her hip.'}
{3: 'A shot rings out, and the first screen shatters.'}
{3: 'Clack, clack, clack. Virtual rounds stream from the chamber, each sharp crack of breaking glass cutting into Adelyde's ears.'}
{3: 'The barrel swings to the last remaining panel—'}
{2: 'Nice to meet you, Adelyde.', 3: '157', 4: 'It's been a long time, Adelyde.', 5: '157'}
{3: 'That familiar translucent figure peeks out from behind the light panel, both hands raised.'}
{3: 'There is no grand entrance, no dramatic flare. Not like a hero arriving to save the day. More like an old friend who has been traveling for years and has finally shown up at the door.'}
{3: 'The barrel stops level with the phantom's face. Ten years, and that person has not changed at all.'}
{3: 'This mysterious phantom sailor always drifts to her side when she is at her lowest.'}
{3: 'Why now? Why always at times like this? How did the phantom even reach her?'}
{3: 'Questions crowd her mind, then fall away just as quickly. She has no strength left to chase them.'}
{3: 'She pauses, looks at the virtual pistol in her hand—'}
{3: 'And she throws it at the figure.'}
{3: 'The pistol arcs through the air, about to pass straight through the translucent figure and clatter to the ground.'}
{3: 'The pistol lands squarely in the figure's grasp. Both of them freeze at once.'}
{2: '(Look down at the pistol in your palm)', 3: '183', 4: '(Give it a squeeze and feel the solid weight)', 5: '183'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: '(You can't touch me, Rusalka, or the cross cannon... but the pistol works?)', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: '(...This is a training simulation. The pistol and everything else here is just data signals synced to my mind.)', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: '(And you're... a kind of signal too.)', 4: '1'}
{3: 'She lifts her head, a spark of light returning to her eyes after a long absence.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You can actually touch things here, physically.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Looks like it.', 3: '194', 4: '(Load the rounds in a clean and quick motion)', 5: '194', 6: 'Ready when you are.', 7: '194'}
{3: 'Adelyde turns to the console and begins typing rapidly into the empty air.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Switch training mode from solo to dual co-op.', 4: '1'}
{1: '13', 2: '>>>>>[WARNING: SELECTED SCENE SET EXCEEDS SAFE TRAINING PARAMETERS]<<<<<', 4: '80', 9: '3'}
{2: '[WARNING: SELECTED SCENE SET EXCEEDS SAFE TRAINING PARAMETERS]'}
{3: 'A flood of light pours in again.'}
{3: 'High above the turbulent winds, a transport aircraft with a gaping hole is plunging toward the earth at two hundred meters per second.'}
{3: 'Wind howls through the breach. The control panel blazes red, and alarms tear through the cabin.'}
{3: 'Those faint, luminous hands are already on the controls. The aircraft's violent roll is gradually being smoothed out.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: '...Fine. I need a clear shooting window in 10 seconds.', 4: '18'}
{3: 'Five seconds later, the aircraft stabilizes. She waits for the exact moment when the drones align on the same plane—'}
{3: 'Gunshots ring out, and both drones burst into fireballs, one after the other.'}
{3: 'The storm rages, and the sea roars without pause.'}
{3: 'Waves towering over a dozen meters slam against the wall beside them again and again. The steel deck beneath their feet groans and tilts. This is a base adrift on the open ocean.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Maintenance tunnel's flooded. We're going over the wall.', 4: '1'}
{2: '(Reach out and take Adelyde's hand)', 3: '300', 4: 'We go together.', 5: '300'}
{3: 'Adelyde clips the safety line in place and takes the extended hand.'}
{3: 'A current of warm strength travels from her arm through her entire body, a feeling far more alive than she has ever known fighting on her own.'}
{3: 'An explosion brings down the electrical shaft, plunging the underground facility into absolute darkness. Helmet lights and tactical visors are both rendered useless.'}
{3: 'A flicker of pale silver breaks through the dark, racing to her side.'}
{3: 'The figure is light itself, moving half a step in front, and wherever the glow touches, the ground is safe.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: '...You know, a little warning would've been nice. About you glowing.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Honestly, I don't glow. Probably just the scenario's effect.', 3: '345'}
{3: 'Adelyde follows the faint light, reading the ground through each footfall, picking her way through rubble and floodwater until the exit's brightness floods toward her.'}
{3: 'Their coordination sharpens with every move, the combat rising to a fierce heat, until they begin vying with each other for kills.'}
{3: 'They have lost track of how many scenes have passed.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: '...You're really gonna fight me on this?', 4: '1'}

{3: 'Round after round, victory through teamwork has become a certainty. They have started competing within their own coordination, but the score stays dead even. Neither is willing to give an inch.'}
{3: 'When the final scene ends, the results screen flares to life.'}
{3: 'The familiar fatigue from a hard session brings a strange comfort. The hollow in her chest remains, but it has stopped trying to consume anything.'}
{3: 'Beside her, the phantom is just as winded. Together, they collapse onto the floor.'}
{3: 'A faint smile crosses Adelyde's lips. She cannot pinpoint exactly what she is feeling happy about, but for some reason, she feels lighter.'}
{3: 'The holographic scene fades away, and fragments of light drift downward like falling snow. The space returns to its familiar form as the training room.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'So where exactly did you train? You're seriously good.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Actually, I learned from you. Believe it or not.', 3: '419'}
{3: 'The familiar resistance returns. Every time she tries to ask about the figure's origins or past, the noise drowns out whatever she hears.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Don't be... I can tell it's not something you can control.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Only what's already happened is free from the laws of time, and only that can be spoken.', 3: '429'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'I figured as much... I've got an idea. Came up with it while you were away.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'I ask, and you respond with body language. Nod or shake your head, that kind of thing.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'That might get blocked too, you know.', 3: '434'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'The way you moved in combat... Are you military?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You've been looking for something... Did you find it?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The figure begins to blur, as though the question has touched something beyond reach. But Adelyde still catches the motion.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'So you found part of it, but you're still searching for the rest?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'With her guess confirmed, Adelyde feels a flicker of curiosity.'}
{3: 'The question leaves her mouth, and regret follows immediately. She suddenly realizes that this is not a matter body language can address.'}
{3: 'Adelyde feels something unfamiliar stir within her.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'And the part you're still looking for?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'She decides to push her luck, asking another question that defies physical reply.'}
{3: 'Regret arrives on its heels. The figure shudders violently, as though caught in a current of corrupted data. That person is about to vanish.'}
{3: 'Adelyde's words come faster than they ever have. She does not want the phantom to leave.'}
{3: 'The figure moves once more, fighting against the surging tide. The gesture is resolute.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'The part you found is me... and the part you haven't... is also me?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Adelyde takes a slow breath. What she is about to say will reach beyond her own understanding.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You're not looking for me now, but the future me?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Time travel... I don't think it's impossible down the line.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'A while back, Professor Dominik gave a lecture on string theory at the Atlantic Eye.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Matter can't break light speed, but information might be different. Theoretically, string vibrations could carry high-density information across time...', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'What's it like in the future? Is it a peaceful world?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'A faint smile tugs at the corners of her mouth, as though she had known all along.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You don't seem exactly calm about it. If things were really peaceful, you wouldn't end up with me here.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'A faint smile tugs at the corners of her mouth, as though she had known all along.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'If a bad future is bound to happen, I'd rather meet it on my own two feet.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'She remembers Port A054, and the memory leaves a faint ache in her gaze, quickly suppressed.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Unless there's really something we can do about it.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'And that's the moment I'm here waiting for.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You have to go back to the future, right?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Back to the future, to your side.', 3: '514', 4: '(Nod)', 5: '519'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Think about it. You've been drifting around me for ten years, and that moment still hasn't come.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'That means I still don't have what it takes to help you. I couldn't even keep one friend today.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'You ran this simulation with me, and I can't even thank you properly. We can't touch. I can't even buy you a meal.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'How long are you going to have to wait, stuck with someone like me?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'A heavy bitterness rises in her chest, and Adelyde speaks more than she usually does, the words spilling out without restraint.'}
{2: 'I'm here with you not because I'm expecting anything from you.', 3: '528'}
{2: 'I do have a mission to complete.', 3: '531'}
{2: 'But that doesn't mean everyone I meet has to give something up for it.', 3: '532'}
{2: 'I drift around, searching, crossing through time—', 3: '534'}
{2: 'So that people won't have to give anything up anymore.', 3: '535'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: '...The sea's so big, and you're crossing it by yourself?', 4: '1'}
{2: 'There are plenty of others sailing with me.', 3: '540'}
{2: 'Even if they're not right here next to me.', 3: '541'}
{2: 'Where I'm from, we've got a saying—', 3: '542'}
{2: 'I do not walk alone, and I will never give up.', 3: '543'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: '...I do not walk alone, and I will never give up.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'She murmurs the words again, turning them over in her mind, testing their weight.'}
{3: 'The shimmering phantom slowly sits up and extends a hand toward her. It is a gesture she knows well: the offer to pull her to her feet.'}
{2: 'But that's not going to stop me from reaching out.', 3: '553'}
{3: 'Adelyde looks at the hand waiting in the air.'}
{3: 'That hand once tried to steady her when she was about to fall. It caught nothing, but she never toppled.'}
{3: 'Slowly, she lifts her own hand and reaches toward it.'}
{3: 'A moment before their fingers can touch, the faint gray figure gradually fades away.'}
{3: 'Like morning mist dissolving into the soft sunlight pouring through.'}
{3: 'The training room falls quiet again. Only the white ceiling lights remain, along with her hand, still outstretched in the air.'}
{3: 'She plants her other palm on the ground and lifts herself up.'}
{3: 'She sits down at the console and opens her terminal.'}
{3: 'An unread email sits at the top of her inbox, where it has remained for a week.'}
{1: '11', 2: '<color=#ffffffff><size=35>[F.O.S. Military Command College: Special Admissions Guide]</size></color>', 3: '750', 4: '50', 9: '3', 10: '1', 11: '1'}
{2: '[F.O.S. Military Command College: Special Admissions Guide]'}
{3: 'Adelyde has heard of this academy, founded by Dominik and assembled from elite minds across the globe.'}
{3: 'Within it, the purest ideals and brightest glories of the Golden Age are preserved.'}
{3: 'She had avoided opening the mail because this path was never part of the blueprint for a family heir.'}

{3: 'The century-long friendship between the four great families, the joint education at the Atlantic Eye, the dream shared by all of humanity in the Golden Age... all of it had quietly promised her a future that was not so terrible.'}
{3: 'But Adelyde must still move forward, toward a place where she can look ahead.'}
{3: 'She opens the email, scrolling through department listings, admission requirements, and reviews from past students... She keeps going until she reaches the very bottom.'}
{3: 'At the very bottom of the mail, a single line stands out:'}
{1: '[I do not walk alone, and I will never give up.]', 3: '55'}
{2: '[I do not walk alone, and I will never give up.]'}
{3: 'It is F.O.S.'s message to every student who will one day walk its halls.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'So that's where you came from, sailor.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Her hand drifts to her chest. The endless void that had been there just hours ago finally takes shape. It is not a void at all, she realizes, but a question she has been carrying all along:'}
{3: 'Quietly, Adelyde saves the email deep in her terminal, placing it in the same folder as her copy of Notes on Caring for Mom.'}
{3: 'Then she rises and walks to the far end of the manor, where one room's light still glows through the winter night.'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'I've got so much to tell you about today.', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'About Arakna, about my teacher... and about this sailor, and a saying I learned today.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The pathway closes. The clamor of the world pulls back like a retreating tide, and the golden current folds around you once again.'}

{3: 'Ten years have passed. For you, it felt little more than a few drifts on the tide. For that child, it was the entire journey from staring through a porthole to standing here now, worn with scars.'}
{3: 'She has lost a dear friend, broken with her family, shattered her perfect scores on the light panels with her own hands, and found new questions and a new path.'}
{1: 'She no longer needs anyone to show her the way.', 3: '55'}
{2: 'She no longer needs anyone to show her the way.'}
{2: 'If anything, she's the one who handed me the last piece I was missing.', 3: '653'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Adelyde', 3: 'Matter can't break light speed, but information might be different. Theoretically, string vibrations could carry high-density information across time...', 4: '1'}
{3: 'And at this moment, you fit the definition of information perfectly... A fragment of information, drifting across time and space.'}
{1: 'One, Ananke seems to transmit only when running at maximum output. You will have to wait for the readings to climb back to their peak.', 5: '1'}
{1: 'Two, Ananke is a safety mechanism. For the most part, it slumbers, stirred only when the Atlantic Eye encounters a grave crisis.', 5: '1'}
{1: 'Three, according to the history you know, Ananke has reached full capacity only twice in more than three decades.', 5: '1', 7: '1'}
{3: 'The first was the moon rock strike. And the second—'}
{3: 'Further down this timeline, there is only one moment when Ananke will peak again: the instant the Atlantic Calamity begins.'}
{3: 'Your path home leads straight into the darkest time of her life. To find your way back to the "present," you must stand at the very center of that calamity.'}
{3: 'Golden strings of light emerge from all around you, weaving into words that rest calm and still.'}
{2: 'You're the one who's been opening those pathways for me, right?', 3: '684'}
{1: '"There are still narrow passages in this current. I only pointed you toward them."', 3: '50'}
{2: '"There are still narrow passages in this current. I only pointed you toward them."'}
{1: '"Just enough to let you meet that child."', 3: '50'}
{2: '"Just enough to let you meet that child."'}
{2: 'Then can you get me back to the future?', 3: '691'}
{1: '"That passage is broken. You'll have to walk it and open it yourself."', 3: '50'}
{2: '"That passage is broken. You'll have to walk it and open it yourself."'}
{3: 'It seems you have only one choice left: go to the site where the calamity will fall.'}
{3: 'Yet as the path home sharpens into focus, another question rises with increasing urgency, darker and more insistent.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Rusalka', 3: 'Help us bring back the method to unravel the golden threads. Arius trusts you won't disappoint.', 4: '2'}
{2: '(Why did they send me to the past?)', 3: '716', 4: '("The method to unravel the golden threads"... What exactly is he after?)', 5: '716'}
{3: 'Someone has already charted this course. Someone is already waiting at its end. You follow the road they laid, but the hands that shaped it remain hidden from you.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'The strings of light disperse. Deep within the current, a faint gleam kindles again. There lies the way to F.O.S., and the white-haired silhouette that no longer looks back.'}
